passage:
A clear lake became cloudy after years of nearby farming and construction. Fish numbers dropped, and tourists stopped coming.
Scientists tested the water and found too many nutrients flowing into it. These fed algae, which blocked sunlight and reduced oxygen.
The town worked with farmers to reduce runoff and planted grasses near the shore.
Recovery was slow. The lake did not become clear in one season.
Students studying the project learned that environmental damage can happen gradually and repair can take even longer.
A lake is not only a beautiful surface. It is a system. When too much enters it, the whole balance changes.
